title: Claim-next stops reading a worktree's own holds as somebody else's
action: The last reader of the ledger that asks the acting checkout instead of the cell's owner: search handlers_select.rs for `has_foreign_hold` — it is what makes `cells claim-next` skip a cell whose paths carry a foreign hold. After hha-1 the rows for a worktree's cell name that worktree, so claim-next run from MAIN would read a cell's own holds as foreign and refuse to hand it out. Ask hha-1's helper for the candidate cell and compare against that, so a cell is skipped only when the hold belongs to a DIFFERENT work stream. Leave the write-guard alone on purpose (search hooks/write_guard/checks.rs for `find_foreign_holds` to see it): once a row names its real owner, a worker inside that worktree matches it and the deny stops firing, and main being denied a write to that worktree's file is the correct answer, not a bug.

truths: cells claim-next run from main returns a cell whose paths carry holds owned by that cell's own worktree
cells claim-next still skips a cell whose paths carry a hold owned by a different feature's worktree
The write-guard's cross-worktree deny is unchanged

artifacts.substantive: the foreign-hold test resolved through the cell-ownership helper
a red-first case for claim-next over a cell whose own worktree holds its paths, and the still-skipped different-owner case

key_links: claim-next asks who owns the candidate cell before calling a hold foreign
prohibitions: Do not let claim-next hand out a cell whose paths are held by another work stream

trace.outcome: candidate_ok behind cells claim-next now resolves the candidate cell through cell_hold_owner and hands has_foreign_hold that owner instead of the literal acting holder, so a cell whose own worktree holds its paths is no longer read as foreign. has_foreign_hold keeps its signature; hooks/write_guard is untouched. Worker ran the declared suite inside the feature worktree: 1675 passed, 0 failed, 11 ignored (16 suites) - the 1674 base plus exactly the one new case. Red seen first: 'a cell's own worktree holding its paths is not a foreign hold', 0 passed 1 failed.
deviations: commands.test could not be run from this checkout: the change lives on the feature worktree's branch, so a run here would test unchanged code. The evidence recorded is the worker's own full-suite run inside the worktree.
